learning: Across iterations 3 to 10, the 16 mm and 12 mm rows at +/-0.03 m with kp 1.2 and kd 0.4 were the best-supported controller. The +/-0.04 m row at kp 1.2 scored 61.35, so widening is worse. Off-track at max error near 0.06 m remains the binding failure on every development track. The unresolved question is whether slalom oscillation comes from sensing lag, gain or the start of the course, and it was not tested in time.
notes: Final package: the iteration 10 geometry (12 mm, x = -0.03 to 0.03 at y = 0.04) with the iteration 10 controller (kp 1.2, ki 0, kd 0.4, base_speed 1.1, last_direction). It is unchanged, so it should reproduce the 74.80 development score. Slalom oscillation (0.246) is left as the known risk, because an untested controller change would reach the unseen track without any check.
rationale: This is the final iteration, and the package races once on an unseen track with no later development race to check it. The Builder's entity0 holds the iteration 10 geometry: five 12 mm sensors at x = -0.03 to 0.03 in 0.015 m steps, y = 0.04, with wheel_track 0.12, wheel_radius 0.03, body 0.18 x 0.12 and mass 0.7. This is the best raced design (74.80), and its per-track results were oval 72.63, s-bend 77.39 and slalom 74.39. The controller that produced 74.80 in iteration 10 was kp 1.2, ki 0, kd 0.4, base_speed 1.1, weights (-1, -0.5, 0, 0.5, 1) and last_direction line loss. The simulator is deterministic for a fixed geometry and controller, as iterations 3, 5, 6, 7 and 9 showed with identical scores, so this package should reproduce 74.80 on the development tracks. The slalom steering oscillation of 0.246 and line loss of about 1.95 per run are the open risk. I considered a controller-only fix, such as lowering kp or raising kd on the slalom. I did not apply it, because nothing I could change has been raced on this exact layout and there is no later race to check a regression. Any change would reach the unseen track untested. The 74.80 package is the most reliable delivery.
